summary: Tsui Lan Liza Cheung is a Buddhist studies scholar. She earned her PhD at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2013) under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti, having also studied under Toshiichi Endo.

Tsukasa Mizushima is an indologist and historian who earned his degrees, including a doctorate in literature (1992), from the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1979–1995) and the University of Tokyo (1997–2018; Emeritus Professor).

Tsultrim Allione works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under traditional teachers including Chögyam Trungpa, the 16th Karmapa, Apho Rinpoche, Kalu Rinpoche, Abo Rinpoche, and Namkhai Norbu, earned a master's at Antioch University, and founded Tara Mandala in 1993.

Tsultrim Gyatso is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He served as Abbot of Drepung Gomang Dratsang (attested 1987) and as a senior instructor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

Tsultrim Kelsang is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He held positions at the International Buddhist Association (attested 1973), Otani University as lecturer (attested 1984) and professor (attested 1999–2002), and was a guest/open researcher at Ryukoku University in 2015.

Tsuneki Nishiwaki is a scholar of philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tokyo University of Education (ca. 1962–1968) and held professorial posts at Kyoto University (ca. 1994–2007) and Doshisha University (ca. 2007–2014).

Tsuruji Sahoda was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Kyoto University (ca. 1923–1926). He later held academic posts at Osaka University (ca. 1950–1963) and Ritsumeikan University (ca. 1963–1973).
Tsutomu Hatai was an Indology scholar who served as president of the Ayurveda Research Society, succeeding Hiroshi Maruyama (attested 1987).
Tsutomu Horio is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Keiji Nishitani. He served as a professor at Otani University (attested 1990).

Tsutomu Kubo was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo under Raphael von Koeber and earned a doctorate from Tohoku University (1953). He held posts at the University of Tokyo, Tohoku University, and Toyo University.

Tsutomu Yamaguchi is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Hokkaido University and served as a collaborative researcher at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2015, 2026).

Tsuyoshi Yokoyama is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He pursued doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2015–2017) and served as a specially appointed researcher at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2017).
Tsyben Zhamtsarano was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar and linguist. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University in 1902 and later headed the Mongolian Academy of Sciences.

Tu Weiming is a philosopher and Sinologist who studied under Mou Zongsan, Tang Chun-i, and Xu Fuguan, earning degrees from Tunghai, Tokai, and Harvard. He held professorships at Berkeley, Harvard, and Peking University, and directed the Harvard-Yenching Institute.

Tubten Chokyi Dorje studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. His students included Shenphen Nangwa, Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.
Tubten Gyeltsen Ozer studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.

Tubten Nyendrak was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies figure who studied under Shenphen Nangwa, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He taught Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima and Dodrupchen Rinpoche.
Tubten Nyima studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Dodrupchen Rinpoche.
Tubten Tsondru studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, and Khenpo Gangshar. He taught Khenchen Palden Sherab Rinpoche and Ringu Tulku.
Tukaram Ramchandra Laddu was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg until 1912. He held a post at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1920).
